sentences.chinese: 天有四維，地有四瀆。
sentences.literal: Heaven has four sustaining cords (weft/bindings); earth has four great draining channels.
sentences.idiomatic: The sky is hung on four cosmic stays, and the land is gouged by four mighty watercourses that carry the flood away.

sentences.chinese: 八紘之外，名爲八極。
sentences.literal: Outside the eight cords of the world, they are called the eight extremities.
sentences.idiomatic: Beyond the encircling girdle that ropes in the known world lie the eight outermost reaches.

sentences.chinese: 地不足東南，天不足西北。
sentences.literal: Earth falls short toward the southeast; heaven falls short toward the northwest.
sentences.idiomatic: The ground gives way to the southeast, while the empyrean gapes widest toward the northwest.

sentences.chinese: 八極之廣，東西二億三萬一千三百里，南北二億三萬一千三百里。
sentences.literal: The breadth of the eight extremities: east and west, two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li; north and south, likewise two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li.
sentences.idiomatic: From the eastern pole to the western spans two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li—and the same measure runs from south to north.

sentences.chinese: 自地至天，半八極之數，自下亦如之。
sentences.literal: From earth to heaven is half the tally of the eight extremities; from below upward it is likewise.
sentences.idiomatic: The vault above measured half the span of the Eight Poles, and the same depth echoed below.

sentences.chinese: 昔黃帝令豎亥步自東極，至于西極，五億十萬九千八百八步。
sentences.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor ordered Shu Hai to pace from the eastern extremity to the western extremity: five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight paces.
sentences.idiomatic: Once the Yellow Emperor bade Shu Hai stride from sunrise to sunset; the tally came to five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight measured paces.

sentences.chinese: 史臣案，凡周天積百七萬九百一十三里，徑三十五萬六千九百七十里。
sentences.literal: The court historiographers ascertain: in all the circumference of heaven totals one million seventy thousand nine hundred thirteen li; the diameter is three hundred fifty-six thousand nine hundred seventy li.
sentences.idiomatic: Court mathematicians reckoned heaven's circuit at 1,070,913 li and its diameter at 356,970 li.

sentences.chinese: 所謂南北爲經，東西爲緯。
sentences.literal: That which is called: north-south as warp, east-west as weft.
sentences.idiomatic: This is what is meant by naming north-south the warp and east-west the weft.

sentences.chinese: 天有十二次，日月之所躔；
sentences.literal: Heaven has twelve celestial lodges; they are where the sun and moon tread their circuits;
sentences.idiomatic: Twelve lunar lodges score the sky—the highway of sun and moon;

sentences.chinese: 地有十二辰，王侯之所國也。
sentences.literal: earth has twelve earthly branches; they are where kings and marquises establish states.
sentences.idiomatic: twelve earthly divisions underpin the map where lords and princes plant their altars of soil and grain.

sentences.chinese: 或因生得姓，因功命土，祁、酉、燕、齊，在乎茲域。
sentences.literal: Some by birth obtain surnames, by merit receive land; Qi, You, Yan, and Qi lie within this region.
sentences.idiomatic: Some clans took names from ancestral seats, others earned fiefs for deeds done—and the old domains of Qi, You, Yan, and Qi all fall inside these bounds.

sentences.chinese: 昔黃帝旁行天下，方制萬里，得百里之國萬區，則《周易》所謂「首出庶物，萬國咸寧」者也。
sentences.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor traveled the realm in all directions, regulated a square of ten thousand li, and obtained ten thousand regions of hundred-li states—this is what the Zhou Yi calls "first emerging among the myriad things; the myriad states all attain tranquility."
sentences.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor quartered the realm, squared a domain ten thousand li on a side, and carved it into ten thousand hundred-li polities—the very epoch the Book of Changes extols when it says, "He who rises first above the throng brings every kingdom to rest."

sentences.chinese: 昔在帝堯，協和萬邦，制八家爲鄰，三鄰爲朋，三朋爲里，五里爲邑，十邑爲都，十都爲師，州十有二師焉。
sentences.literal: Formerly under Emperor Yao he harmonized the myriad states; he regulated: eight households form a neighborhood, three neighborhoods form a peng, three peng form a li, five li form a yi, ten yi form a du, ten du form a shi, and a province has twelve shi.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Yao the countries learned concord, and government knit tight: eight families made a street, three streets a cluster, three clusters a ward, five wards a market town, ten such towns a greater burgh, ten burghs a canton, and twelve cantons stitched one province.

sentences.chinese: 夏后氏東漸于海，西被于流沙，南浮于江，而朔南暨聲教，窮豎亥所步，莫不率俾，會群臣於塗山，執玉帛者萬國。
sentences.literal: The house of Xia eastward reached to the sea, westward extended to the flowing sands, southward floated on the Jiang; north and south likewise were united by culture and teaching, exhausting where Shu Hai had paced; none failed to follow and obey; they assembled the host of lords at Tu Shan; those bearing jade and silk were ten thousand states.
sentences.idiomatic: The Xia stretched east until the tide foamed at their feet, west to the shifting sands, south along the great rivers, until their transforming influence ran from pole to pole as far as Shu Hai had ever measured; none refused homage. At Mount Tu they gathered the lords, and ten thousand courts arrived with jade disks and silk.

sentences.chinese: 於是九州之內，作爲五服。
sentences.literal: Thereupon within the nine provinces they established the five domains (fu).
sentences.idiomatic: Within the Nine Provinces they layered five concentric belts of fealty.

sentences.chinese: 天子之國，內五百里甸服，百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven's state: the inner five hundred li is the royal domain; at one hundred li tribute is delivered as bound sheaves in the husk; at two hundred li sickle-cut ears; at three hundred li straw and corvée service; at four hundred li millet; at five hundred li rice.
sentences.idiomatic: Around the capital ran five hundred li of royal fields: the inner ring sent whole stalks bundled, the next matured heads, the third straw and labor, the fourth threshed grain, the outermost polished rice for the palace kettle.

sentences.chinese: 甸服外五百里侯服，百里采，二百里任，三百里候。
sentences.literal: Outside the royal domain, five hundred li of marquis-domain: one hundred li of estates, two hundred li of appointments, three hundred li of garrison/watch.
sentences.idiomatic: Beyond that stretched another five hundred li of baronial land: the first hundred fed royal manors, the next two hundred supplied ministers of trust, the outer three hundred patrolled the marches.

sentences.chinese: 侯服外五百里綏服，三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
sentences.literal: Outside the marquis-domain, five hundred li of pacification-domain: three hundred li for adjusting civil teaching and rites, two hundred li for vigorous martial guard.
sentences.idiomatic: Next came five hundred li meant to "soothe": three hundred for schools and rites, two hundred bristling with spears that guarded the cordon.

sentences.chinese: 綏服外五百里要服，三百里夷，二百里蔡。
sentences.literal: Outside the pacification-domain, five hundred li of binding-domain: three hundred li of outer Yi, two hundred li of Cai.
sentences.idiomatic: Outside the pacified belt lay five hundred li of "treaty" ground—three hundred li of loosely ruled bordermen, two hundred more under banishment law.

sentences.chinese: 要服外五百里荒服，三百里蠻，二百里流。
sentences.literal: Outside the binding-domain, five hundred li of wild-domain: three hundred li of Man, two hundred li of exile-flow.
sentences.idiomatic: The rim was five hundred li of wilderness—three hundred left to rough hill tribes, two hundred reserved for the river of banishment.

sentences.chinese: 訖于四海，弼成五服，五服至于五千里。
sentences.literal: Reaching to the four seas, they assisted in completing the five domains; the five domains extend to five thousand li.
sentences.idiomatic: The pattern ran to the four seas, the five girdles locked in place, a full five thousand li from throne to tide-line.

sentences.chinese: 夏德中微，遇有窮之亂。
sentences.literal: Midway Xia's virtue withered; it encountered the disorder of Youqiong.
sentences.idiomatic: Halfway through their age the Xia lost heart, and the realm reeled beneath Youqiong's revolt.

sentences.chinese: 少康中興，不失舊物。
sentences.literal: Shaokang raised a restoration; he did not lose the old inheritance.
sentences.idiomatic: Shaokang rallied the line and never surrendered the ancestral cauldrons.

sentences.chinese: 自孔甲之後，以至于桀，諸侯相兼，其能存者三千餘國，方於塗山，十損其七矣。
sentences.literal: From Kong Jia onward, down to Jie, the feudal lords mutually annexed; those able to survive numbered a bit more than three thousand states; compared to Mount Tu, ten lost seven.
sentences.idiomatic: From Kong Jia to tyrant Jie the lords devoured one another until barely three thousand states remained—seven in ten had vanished since the great conference at Mount Tu.

sentences.chinese: 成湯敗桀於焦，遷鼎於亳，伊摯、仲虺之徒，大明憲典。
sentences.literal: Cheng Tang defeated Jie at Jiao, moved the cauldrons to Bo; men such as Yi Zhi and Zhong Hui greatly clarified statutes and models.
sentences.idiomatic: Cheng Tang broke Jie at Jiao and carried the tripods to Bo; ministers like Yi Yin and Zhong Hui lit clear lamps of law and precedent.

sentences.chinese: 王者之制爵祿，公侯伯子男凡五等。
sentences.literal: The king's system of enfeoffing ranks and salaries: duke, marquis, earl, viscount, baron—in all five grades.
sentences.idiomatic: Royal custom fixed five noble ranks—from duke down to baron—each with its stipend.

sentences.chinese: 天子之田方千里，公侯田方百里，伯七十里，子男五十里。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven's field is a square of a thousand li; duke and marquis, a square of a hundred li; earl, seventy li; viscount and baron, fifty li.
sentences.idiomatic: The king measured a thousand li square; dukes and marquises a hundred, earls seventy, viscounts and barons a bare fifty on a side.

sentences.chinese: 不能五十里者，不達於天子，附於諸侯，曰附庸。
sentences.literal: Those unable to reach fifty li do not communicate directly with the Son of Heaven; they attach to feudal lords; they are called dependencies.
sentences.idiomatic: Polities shy of fifty li could not seek audience alone; they hung on greater lords as client domains.

sentences.chinese: 凡四海之內九州，州方千里。
sentences.literal: In all, within the four seas are nine provinces; each province is a square of a thousand li.
sentences.idiomatic: Within the four seas lay nine provinces, each a thousand-li square on the chart.

sentences.chinese: 州建百里之國三十，七十里之國六十，五十里之國百有二十，凡二百一十國。
sentences.literal: In a province are established thirty states of a hundred li, sixty states of seventy li, one hundred twenty states of fifty li—in all two hundred ten states.
sentences.idiomatic: Each province raised thirty great hundred-li realms, sixty middling seventy-li counties, and a hundred twenty small fifty-li cells—two hundred ten banners in all.

sentences.chinese: 名山大澤不以封，其餘以爲附庸間田。
sentences.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not used for enfeoffment; the remainder becomes dependencies and interstitial fields.
sentences.idiomatic: Crown peaks and imperial bogs never left the king's ledger; leftover patches became vassal pockets and buffer strips.

sentences.chinese: 八州，州二百一十國。
sentences.literal: Eight provinces—each province two hundred ten states.
sentences.idiomatic: Eight of the nine provinces repeated that pattern—two hundred ten states apiece.

sentences.chinese: 天子之縣內，百里之國九，七十里之國二十有一，五十里之國六十有三，凡九十三國。
sentences.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's direct counties: nine states of a hundred li, twenty-one states of seventy li, sixty-three states of fifty li—in all ninety-three states.
sentences.idiomatic: Inside the royal demesne itself stood nine hundred-li seats, twenty-one seventy-li manors, and sixty-three fifty-li plots—ninety-three realms devoted to the throne.

sentences.chinese: 名山大澤不以班，其餘以祿士，以爲間田。
sentences.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not parceled out in enfeoffment; the remainder is used to salary officers and becomes interstitial fields.
sentences.idiomatic: Sacred heights and royal marshes were never fiefed away; the scraps paid stipendiary officials and plugged holes between grants.

sentences.chinese: 凡九州，千七百七十三國。
sentences.literal: In all the nine provinces: one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.
sentences.idiomatic: Across the Nine Provinces the tallies listed one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.

sentences.chinese: 天子之元士，諸侯之附庸，不與。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven's chief knights and the feudal lords' dependencies are not included.
sentences.idiomatic: The count omits the king's senior householders and the petty clients of great barons.

sentences.chinese: 天子百里之內以供官，千里之內以爲御，千里之外設方伯。
sentences.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's hundred li, for supplying officials; within a thousand li, for court provision; beyond a thousand li, regional hegemons are appointed.
sentences.idiomatic: The inner hundred li fed the bureaucracy, the thousand li stocked palace service, and beyond that the king set regional elders to rule in his stead.

sentences.chinese: 五國以爲屬，屬有長；
sentences.literal: Five states form a dependency-group; a dependency-group has a chief.
sentences.idiomatic: Five states formed a dependency cluster led by a chief.

sentences.chinese: 十國以爲連，連有帥；
sentences.literal: Ten states form a chain; a chain has a commander.
sentences.idiomatic: Ten states formed a league placed under a captain.

sentences.chinese: 三十國以爲卒，卒有正；
sentences.literal: Thirty states form a corps; a corps has a director.
sentences.idiomatic: Thirty states formed a corps overseen by a senior marshal.

sentences.chinese: 二百一十國以爲州，州有伯。
sentences.literal: Two hundred ten states form a province; a province has a bo.
sentences.idiomatic: Two hundred ten states formed a province ruled by a regional elder.

sentences.chinese: 八州，八伯，五十六正，百六十八帥，三百三十六長。
sentences.literal: Eight provinces: eight bo, fifty-six directors, one hundred sixty-eight commanders, three hundred thirty-six chiefs.
sentences.idiomatic: Eight provinces meant eight great lords, fifty-six marshals, one hundred sixty-eight captains, and three hundred thirty-six village heads.

sentences.chinese: 八伯各以其屬屬於天子之老二人，分天下爲左右，曰二伯。
sentences.literal: Each of the eight bo with his dependents attaches to two elders of the Son of Heaven; they divide the realm into left and right, called the two bo.
sentences.idiomatic: Each provincial lord knelt to one of the king's two senior regents, splitting the world into eastern and western halves—the Two Chiefs of high Zhou.

sentences.chinese: 千里之內曰甸，千里之外曰采，曰流。
sentences.literal: Within a thousand li is called dian; beyond a thousand li is called cai and liu.
sentences.idiomatic: Inside the thousand-li cordon lay the royal hearths; outside stretched ministerial estates and the flowing lands of exile.

sentences.chinese: 天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國，國三人。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven causes his great officers to be triple overseers; they oversee in the regional hegemons' states; three men per state.
sentences.idiomatic: The king posted three-man inspectorates in every regional capital to eye the barons for him.

sentences.chinese: 天子之縣，內，諸侯祿也；
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven's counties: inwardly, they are stipendiary fiefs for feudal lords.
sentences.idiomatic: Domains hugging the throne were stipendiary grants to great lords.

sentences.chinese: 外，諸侯嗣也。
sentences.literal: Outwardly, they are inheriting lineages of feudal lords.
sentences.idiomatic: Those farther out settled into noble lines handed down through inheritance.

sentences.chinese: 武王歸豐，監於二代，設爵惟五，分土惟三。
sentences.literal: King Wu returned to Feng, examined the two dynasties, established ranks only five, divided land only three grades.
sentences.idiomatic: King Wu withdrew to Feng, studied Xia and Shang, fixed five noble rows, and sorted fief size into three steps.

sentences.chinese: 封同姓五十餘國，周公、康叔建於魯衛，各數百里。
sentences.literal: He enfeoffed kinsmen fifty-odd states; the Duke of Zhou and Kang Shu were established at Lu and Wei, each several hundred li.
sentences.idiomatic: He planted more than fifty Zhou princes across the map—the Duke of Zhou at Lu, Kang Shu at Wei—each commanding several hundred li.

sentences.chinese: 太公封於齊，表東海者也。
sentences.literal: Grand Duke Tai was enfeoffed at Qi—he who screens the eastern sea.
sentences.idiomatic: Tai Gong took Qi as his shield against the eastern tide.

sentences.chinese: 凡一千八百國，布列於五千里內。
sentences.literal: In all one thousand eight hundred states, arrayed within five thousand li.
sentences.idiomatic: Eighteen hundred realms checkered the five-thousand-li heartland.

sentences.chinese: 而太昊、黃帝之後，唐虞侯伯猶存。
sentences.literal: Moreover descendants of Taihao and the Yellow Emperor—Tang-Yao era marquises and earls—still survived.
sentences.idiomatic: Lines sprung from Taihao and the Yellow Emperor, marquises who remembered Yao and Shun, still clung to titles in that new Zhou dawn.

sentences.chinese: 大司徒以諸公之地封疆方五百里，其食者半；
sentences.literal: The grand steward: the lands of the dukes have boundaries a square of five hundred li; of it half provides revenue.
sentences.idiomatic: The Minister of Education carved dukes five hundred li square but let them tax only half the soil;

sentences.chinese: 諸侯之地方四百里，其食者參之一；
sentences.literal: The lands of marquises are four hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
sentences.idiomatic: marquises held four hundred li yet drew a third to their kitchens;

sentences.chinese: 諸伯之地方三百里，其食者參之一；
sentences.literal: The lands of earls are three hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
sentences.idiomatic: earls kept three hundred li with the same third rule;

sentences.chinese: 諸子之地方二百里，其食者四之一；
sentences.literal: The lands of viscounts are two hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
sentences.idiomatic: viscounts two hundred li but spent only a quarter;

sentences.chinese: 諸男之地方百里，其食者四之一。
sentences.literal: The lands of barons are a hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
sentences.idiomatic: barons a bare hundred li yet owned a quarter of the yield.

sentences.chinese: 不易之地家百畝，一易之地家二百畝，再易之地家三百畝。
sentences.literal: On land that does not rotate, a household receives a hundred mu; on land rotated once, two hundred mu; on land rotated twice, three hundred mu.
sentences.idiomatic: Permanent fields granted a household a hundred mu, once-fallow soil two hundred, and thrice-tired ground three hundred so the tax base stayed even.

sentences.chinese: 五家爲比，使之相保；
sentences.literal: Five households form a bi; they are caused mutually to guarantee.
sentences.idiomatic: Five families swore mutual bail;

sentences.chinese: 五比爲閭，使之相受；
sentences.literal: Five bi form a lü; they are caused mutually to shelter.
sentences.idiomatic: five such rings a lane that housed the homeless;

sentences.chinese: 四閭爲族，使之相葬；
sentences.literal: Four lü form a zu; they are caused mutually to bury.
sentences.idiomatic: four lanes a clan burying its dead together;

sentences.chinese: 五族爲黨，使之相救；
sentences.literal: Five zu form a dang; they are caused mutually to rescue.
sentences.idiomatic: five clans a company that rushed to fires and raids;

sentences.chinese: 五黨爲州，使之相賙；
sentences.literal: Five dang form a zhou; they are caused mutually to relieve.
sentences.idiomatic: five companies a canton pooling famine grain;

sentences.chinese: 五州爲鄉，使之相賓。
sentences.literal: Five zhou form a xiang; they are caused mutually to observe guest ritual.
sentences.idiomatic: five cantons a countryside whose elders still bowed in guest-rite.

sentences.chinese: 小司徒以五人爲伍，五伍爲兩，四兩爲卒，五卒爲旅，五旅爲師，五師爲軍。
sentences.literal: The lesser steward: by five men a squad, five squads a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a division, five divisions an army.
sentences.idiomatic: The junior steward stacked squads: five men a file, five files a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a host, five hosts the full army.

sentences.chinese: 以起軍旅，以作田役，以比追胥，以令貢賦。
sentences.literal: By this raise armies, perform field labor and corvée, compare pursuit and night patrol, order tribute and taxes.
sentences.idiomatic: Those ladders raised campaigns, drafted ditch gangs, mustered night watchmen, and split the grain and corvée rolls.

sentences.chinese: 乃經土地而井牧其田野，九夫爲井，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸，四甸爲縣，四縣爲都。
sentences.literal: Then they surveyed land and well-and-pastured the fields and wilds: nine husbands a well, four wells a settlement, four settlements a mound, four mounds a dian, four dian a county, four counties a metropolis.
sentences.idiomatic: Surveyors laid the well-net: nine farmers to a well, four wells a hamlet, four hamlets a hill-girdle, four hill-girdles a parcel, four parcels a county, four counties a great city.

sentences.chinese: 遺人則十里有廬，廬有飲食。
sentences.literal: The supply officer: then every ten li has a hut; the hut has drink and food.
sentences.idiomatic: Wayfarers found a lodge every ten li with water and a warm bowl.

sentences.chinese: 三十里有宿，宿有路室，路室有委。
sentences.literal: Every thirty li has a lodging; the lodging has roadside chambers; the roadside chambers have stored provisions.
sentences.idiomatic: Every thirty li brought a full station, roadside cells, and stacked grain.

sentences.chinese: 五十里有市，市有候，候有館，館有積。
sentences.literal: Every fifty li has a market; the market has a post; the post has a lodge; the lodge has accumulations.
sentences.idiomatic: Every fifty li markets bustled with guard posts, guest halls, and piled stores.

sentences.chinese: 遂人則五家爲鄰，五鄰爲里，四里爲酇，五酇爲鄙，五鄙爲縣，五縣爲遂。
sentences.literal: The field officer: five households form lin, five lin a li, four li a zan, five zan a bi, five bi a county, five counties a sui.
sentences.idiomatic: Rural marshals wove five homes into a lane, five lanes a hamlet, four hamlets a township, five townships a patch, five patches a county, five counties a sui belt.

sentences.chinese: 大司馬以九畿之籍，施邦國之政。
sentences.literal: The grand marshal, by the registers of the nine ji, applies governance to the states.
sentences.idiomatic: The war minister read the nine belts girding Wangcheng and from them spun every lord's marching orders.

sentences.chinese: 方千里曰國畿，其外方五百里曰侯畿，又其外方五百里曰甸畿，又其外方五百里曰男畿，又其外方五百里曰采畿，又其外方五百里曰衛畿，又其外方五百里曰蠻畿，又其外方五百里曰夷畿，又其外方五百里曰鎮畿，又其外方五百里曰藩畿。
sentences.literal: A square of a thousand li is called the royal ji; its outer square of five hundred li is the marquis ji; again outside five hundred li is the dian ji; again outside five hundred li is the male-rank ji; again outside five hundred li is the stipend ji; again outside five hundred li is the guard ji; again outside five hundred li is the man ji; again outside five hundred li is the yi ji; again outside five hundred li is the garrison ji; again outside five hundred li is the vassal-screen ji.
sentences.idiomatic: The capital sat in a thousand-li square; then nine half-thousand-li rings unrolled—baronial fields, royal estates, male fiefs, salary lands, guard strips, southern wilds, eastern wilds, garrison marches, and a final curtain of outer vassals.

sentences.chinese: 〈畿，田限也。
sentences.literal: 〈Ji means the field limit.
sentences.idiomatic: The marginal note explains that ji denotes the border of taxable fields.

sentences.chinese: 自王城以外，面五千里爲界，有分限者九也。〉
sentences.literal: From outside the royal city, on each face five thousand li is the boundary; there are nine division-limits.〉
sentences.idiomatic: It adds that from the royal walls each quarter runs five thousand li, ringed by nine stepped partitions.

sentences.chinese: 于時治致太平，政稱刑措，民口千三百七十一萬四千九百三十三，蓋周之盛者也。
sentences.literal: At that time rule attained the Great Peace, government was called punishments set aside, the people's mouths numbered thirteen million seven hundred fourteen thousand nine hundred thirty-three—this was the height of Zhou.
sentences.idiomatic: That age ripened into the Great Peace, the racks stood empty, and the census inked 13,714,933 names—a Zhou summer at flood tide.

sentences.chinese: 其衰也，則禮樂征伐出自諸侯，強吞弱而眾暴寡。
sentences.literal: In its decline, then rites, music, expeditions, and punitive attacks issued from the feudal lords; the strong swallowed the weak and the many tyrannized the few.
sentences.idiomatic: When it rotted, drums and odes marched under barons' banners, strong states swallowed weak neighbors, and packs harried the lone.

sentences.chinese: 春秋之初，尚有千二百國，迄獲麟之末，二百四十二年，弒君三十六，亡國五十二，諸侯奔走不得保其社稷者不可勝數，而見於春秋經傳者百有七十國焉。
sentences.literal: At the beginning of Spring and Autumn there were still one thousand two hundred states; down to the end of capturing the unicorn, two hundred forty-two years, regicide of lords thirty-six, perished states fifty-two, feudal lords fleeing unable to preserve their altars—uncountable; yet those appearing in the Spring and Autumn classic and commentaries numbered one hundred seventy states.
sentences.idiomatic: Early Spring and Autumn still counted twelve hundred flags; by the day Confucius penned the unicorn's close—two hundred forty-two bloodied years—thirty-six kings had been knifed, fifty-two realms snuffed, and numberless lords fled ruined shrines, though the classic and its gloss remember only one hundred seventy names.

sentences.chinese: 百三十九知其所居，
sentences.literal: One hundred thirty-nine know where they dwelt.
sentences.idiomatic: One hundred thirty-nine of them still have identifiable capitals on the map.

sentences.chinese: 〈魯、邾、鄭、宋、紀、衛、西虢、莒、齊、陳、杞、蔡、邢、郕、晉、薛、許、鄧、秦、曹、楚、隨、黃、梁、虞、鄖、小邾、徐、燕、鄀、麋、舒、庸、郯、萊、吳、越、有窮、三苗、瓜州、有虞、東虢、共、宿、申、夷、向、南燕、滕、凡、戴、息、郜、芮、魏、淳于、穀、巴、州、蓼、羅、賴、牟、葛、譚、蕭、遂、滑、權、鄣、霍、耿、江、冀、弦、道、柏、微、鄫、厲、項、密、任、須句、顓臾、頓、管、雍、畢、豐、邘、應、蔣、茅、胙、夔、介、焦、沈、六、巢、根牟、唐、黎、郇瑕、寒、有鬲、斟灌、斟尋、過、有過、戈、偪陽、邿、鑄、豕韋、唐杜、楊、豳、鄶、觀、扈、邳、胡、黎、大庭、駘、岐、邶、鍾吾、蒲姑、昆吾、房、密須、甲父、鄅、桐、亳、韓、趙。〉
sentences.literal: (Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, Western Guo, Ju, Qi, Chen, Qi, Cai, Xing, Cheng, Jin, Xue, Xu, Deng, Qin, Cao, Chu, Sui, Huang, Liang, Yu, Yun, Lesser Zhu, Xu, Yan, Ruo, Mi, Shu, Yong, Tan, Lai, Wu, Yue, Youqiong, Sanmiao, Guazhou, You Yu, Eastern Guo, Gong, Su, Shen, Yi, Xiang, Southern Yan, Teng, Fan, Dai, Xi, Gao, Rui, Wei, Chunyu, Gu, Ba, Zhou, Liao, Luo, Lai, Mou, Ge, Tan, Xiao, Sui, Hua, Quan, Zhang, Huo, Geng, Jiang, Ji, Xian, Dao, Bo, Wei, Zeng, Li, Xiang, Mi, Ren, Xuqu, Zhuanyu, Dun, Guan, Yong, Bi, Feng, Yu, Ying, Jiang, Mao, Zuo, Kui, Jie, Jiao, Shen, Liu, Chao, Genmou, Tang, Li, Xunxia, Han, Youge, Zhuguan, Zhunxun, Guo, Youguo, Ge, Biyang, Shi, Zhu, Shangwei, Tang Du, Yang, Bin, Kuai, Guan, Hu, Li, Danting, Tai, Qi, Bei, Zhongwu, Pugu, Kunwu, Fang, Mixu, Jiafu, Yu, Tong, Bo, Han, Zhao.)
sentences.idiomatic: among them the old heartlands—Lu, Jin, Qi, Chu, Wu, Yue, Qin, Zheng, Song, and legions of lesser seats that commentators can still triangulate from the text.

sentences.chinese: 三十一國盡亡其處，
sentences.literal: Thirty-one states utterly lost their locations.
sentences.idiomatic: Thirty-one others vanished so completely that their very sites are forgotten.

sentences.chinese: 〈祭、極、荀、賈、貳、軫、絞、於餘丘、陽、箕、英氏、毛、聃、莘、偪、封父、仍、有仍、崇、鄟、庸、姺、奄、商奄、褒姒、蓐、有緡、闕鞏、飂、鬷、窮桑。〉
sentences.literal: (Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, Qiongsang.)
sentences.idiomatic: names like Zhai, Jiao, and Qiongsang surviving only as ghosts in footnotes.

sentences.chinese: 蠻夷戎狄不在其間。
sentences.literal: The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are not among these.
sentences.idiomatic: Southern, eastern, western, and northern tribes were never part of that roll.

sentences.chinese: 五伯迭興，總其盟會。
sentences.literal: The Five Hegemons rose in succession; they oversaw their covenants and assemblies.
sentences.idiomatic: Five overlords rose in turn to chair the league altars and stamp clan oaths.

sentences.chinese: 陵夷至于戰國，遂有七王，
sentences.literal: Declining further, it reached the Warring States; thereupon there were seven kings,
sentences.idiomatic: The slide ran on into the Warring States, and seven crowned powers shouldered the world—

sentences.chinese: 〈韓、魏、趙、燕、齊、秦、楚。〉
sentences.literal: (Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, Chu.)
sentences.idiomatic: Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, and Chu.

sentences.chinese: 又有宋、衛、中山，不斷如綫，如三晉篡奪，亦稱孤也。
sentences.literal: Moreover there were Song, Wei, and Zhongshan, unbroken like a thread; as for the usurpations of the three Jin, they also called themselves orphaned rulers.
sentences.idiomatic: Song, Wei, and Zhongshan still hung by a thread, while the breakaway triplets of Jin stole the mandate yet whimpered that they ruled as orphaned heirs.

sentences.chinese: 《司馬法》廣陳三代，曰：古者六尺爲步，步百爲畝，畝百爲夫，夫三爲屋，屋三爲井。
sentences.literal: The "Sima Fa" broadly expounds the Three Dynasties, saying: In antiquity six chi made a pace, a hundred paces made a mu, a hundred mu made a husband-unit, three husband-units made a roof-cluster, three roof-clusters made a well-field.
sentences.idiomatic: The Military Canons of Sima recount the Three Ages: six feet to the pace, a hundred paces to the survey mu, a hundred mu to a husband's share, three husbands to a cluster, three clusters to the sacred well of nine farms.

sentences.chinese: 井方一里，是爲九夫，八家共之。
sentences.literal: A well is a square of one li; this constitutes nine husband-slots; eight households share it.
sentences.idiomatic: Each well squared a li, carved nine strips, and yoked eight families to its central lord's strip.

sentences.chinese: 一夫一婦受私田百畝，公田十畝，是爲八百八十畝，餘二十畝爲廬舍，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相救。
sentences.literal: One husband one wife receive private fields a hundred mu, public field ten mu—this makes eight hundred eighty mu; the remaining twenty mu are hut-sites; going out and entering they befriend; watching and guarding they assist; in sickness they rescue one another.
sentences.idiomatic: Each couple drew a hundred private mu and ten for the common furrow—880 mu under tillage and twenty for roofs; neighbors pledged friendship at every gate, stood night watch together, and nursed fevers shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.chinese: 民受田，上田夫百畝，中田夫二百畝，下田夫三百畝，歲受耕之，爰自其處。
sentences.literal: The people receive fields: on upper fields a husband has a hundred mu; on middle fields two hundred mu; on lower fields three hundred mu; yearly they receive and till them, shifting accordingly.
sentences.idiomatic: Farmers drew graded plots—one hundred mu on rich soil, two hundred on middling, three hundred on lean—rotating with the seasons as the law nudged them along.

sentences.chinese: 其家眾男爲餘夫，亦以口受田如此。
sentences.literal: The family's multitude of males as surplus husbands likewise by mouth receive fields in this manner.
sentences.idiomatic: Extra grown sons counted as surplus tillers and earned more acreage by the same mouth tally.

sentences.chinese: 士工商家受田，五口乃當農夫一口。
sentences.literal: Scholar, artisan, and merchant households receive fields; five mouths equal one peasant mouth.
sentences.idiomatic: Gentry, craftsmen, and merchants held land too, yet five of their mouths paid as one plowman's share.

sentences.chinese: 有賦有稅，稅謂公田什一及工商衡虞之入也，賦供車馬甲兵士從之役。
sentences.literal: There are fu and shui; shui means the public-field one-tenth and the income of artisans, merchants, weighers, and marsh-keepers; fu supplies chariots, horses, armor, weapons, accompanyers, and corvée.
sentences.idiomatic: Two ledgers ran: "tax" skimmed the lord's tenth and the townsmen who trafficked scales and marshes; "levy" horseshoed chariots, buckled armor, and dragooned footmen.

sentences.chinese: 民年二十受田，六十歸田。
sentences.literal: The people at age twenty receive fields; at sixty they return fields.
sentences.idiomatic: A man took land at twenty and surrendered it at sixty.

sentences.chinese: 種穀必雜五種，以備災旱。
sentences.literal: Planting grain must mix five kinds, to prepare for disaster and drought.
sentences.idiomatic: Every field blended five grains so famine could not kill the harvest whole.

sentences.chinese: 田中不得有樹，以妨五穀。
sentences.literal: In fields there must not be trees, lest they obstruct the five grains.
sentences.idiomatic: Grain land stayed shadeless—no orchard stealing sunlight from the staples.

sentences.chinese: 環廬種桑柘，菜茹有畦，瓜瓠果蓏植於疆埸，雞㹠狗豕無失其時。
sentences.literal: Around huts plant mulberry and zhe; vegetables have beds; melons, gourds, fruits, and berries plant on boundaries; chickens, pigs, dogs, and swine—do not miss their seasons.
sentences.idiomatic: Mulberries hugged each roof, kitchen gardens squared their rows, melons straggled along the headlands, and every yard timed its fowl and hogs to the turning moons.

sentences.chinese: 閭有序，鄉有庠，序以明教，庠以行禮。
sentences.literal: A lü has a village school; a xiang has a hall; the village school clarifies teaching; the hall conducts rites.
sentences.idiomatic: Each lane kept a school where royal lessons shone, each district a hall where elders rehearsed ceremony.

sentences.chinese: 司馬之法，官設六軍之眾，因井田而制軍。
sentences.literal: The Sima method: officials establish the mass of six armies; according to well-fields they regulate armies.
sentences.idiomatic: The war statutes called up six hosts, threading regiment on regiment straight from the well-field grid.
